liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Only about three minutes of Let It Grow survive on this tape before it cuts off [9]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer finds this Sugaree more mature than before, though not especially vibrant [11]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Minglewood bland and low-fat, though crunchy [11]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Reviewer thinks Ramble On Rose tends to plod, with effort and intent present but little payoff [11]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer hears the China intro as a band still searching for its second-set footing [13]
- **Hey Jude Refrain** (1 review): The return of the Hey Jude coda made the crowd erupt [18]
- **Stuck Inside Of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again** (1 review): Reviewer says this was the band's first Memphis Blues Again outside of backing Dylan [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd88-03-17 t01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-03-17 t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-03-17 t03 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-03-17 t04 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-03-17 t05 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-03-17 t06 Memphis Blues Again**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-03-17 t07 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd88-03-17 t08 Let It Grow**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-03-17.141884.ultramatrix.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 143 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd88-03-17.sbd.samaritano.21297.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 135 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [7]
- **gd1988-03-17.sbd.unknown.13602.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 128 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [8]. Said about its sound: Two seconds of Ramble On Rose are missing, and most of Let It Grow is cut [8]
- **gd1988-03-17.sbd.miller.91156.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 143 min; rated 2.5/5 by 4 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls Kaiser shows as relaxed, casual Bay Area home turf, with the hall getting very hot [10]
- This was one of seven Kaiser shows in thirty days, following Valentine's and Mardi Gras shows [16]
- A drunk friend, Lodghead, shouted "Hey Shaun" during the quiet Hamza El Din chant, and about 100 people stared [20]
- Reviewer remembers volleyball and greenery outside the venue [20]
- Reviewer, who attended, thought the show average with a typical setlist apart from the Hey Jude coda and Memphis Blues [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-03-17.141884.ultramatrix.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Master UltraMatrix PCM > PCM; Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (wav 16-bit/44.1k)>… [1]. Also: A soundboard master cassette supplies Let It Grow from 2:42 to its end, plus the set break [1]
- **gd88-03-17.sbd.samaritano.21297.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard->DAT Master->DAT. DAT->ZA2->.wav->mkw->SHN. Transfer and SHN by Joe Samaritano [7]
- **gd1988-03-17.sbd.unknown.13602.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Robert Stevens; source: Master DAT>DATS>CDR>EAC>SHN [8]. Also: A stranger made the DAT to CDR transfer for the uploader, Robert [8]
- **gd1988-03-17.sbd.miller.91156.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat (48k) D [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1988-03-17 Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center, Oakland, CA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/08/grateful-dead-1988-03-17-henry-j-kaiser.html) [22]
